opening.argument: The speaker presents a beginner-oriented lesson in building a responsive HTML5 website from scratch, using a fictional web-design site to teach HTML and CSS. The demonstration shows the page alongside its code, and the speaker explains responsive behavior through media queries. The newsletter form is expressly identified as a display element: it will not work, and no backend programming is being done. Those observable details make the site and its form parts of a coding exercise, not a financial offer or a request for data access. Nothing in the demonstrated form supports treating it as a functioning collection mechanism.

citations.quote: Hey guys in this tutorial we're going to be building an HTML5 responsive website from scratch.
So we're going to go over the HTML5 Semantic Tags and HTML in general and build a fairly decent small website for a web design company
Now, this form isn't going to work. We're not doing any backend programming. It's just, you know is just a display form.
Now, the way that we do this is through media queries.
